topicName: Extraction of Iron from its Ore
description: This topic covers how iron is extracted from its main ore, haematite, using the blast furnace process. It examines the roles of coke, limestone and carbon monoxide in reducing iron oxide and removing impurities, and explains the difference between the pig iron produced and the steel made from it.

mcq.questionText: A naturally occurring rock or mineral from which a metal can be economically extracted is called a(n):
mcq.explanation: A naturally occurring rock or mineral from which a metal can be economically extracted is called an ore. Exam Tip: Ores contain enough of the metal (usually as a compound) to make extraction worthwhile.

mcq.questionText: The main ore of iron, rich in iron(III) oxide, is called:
mcq.explanation: Haematite (Fe2O3) is the principal ore of iron, rich in iron(III) oxide, and is the main industrial source of the metal. Exam Tip: Haematite (iron(III) oxide) is reddish-brown and the primary source of iron industrially.

mcq.questionText: The large industrial furnace used to extract iron from its ore is called a:
mcq.explanation: The blast furnace is the large industrial furnace used to extract iron from its ore, where iron ore, coke and limestone are heated together. Exam Tip: The blast furnace is a tall structure where iron ore, coke and limestone are heated together.

mcq.questionText: In the blast furnace, the raw materials fed in at the top include iron ore, coke and:
mcq.explanation: The three main raw materials fed into the blast furnace are iron ore (source of iron), coke (fuel and reducing agent) and limestone (removes impurities). Exam Tip: Three key raw materials: iron ore (the source of iron), coke (fuel and reducing agent), limestone (removes impurities).

mcq.questionText: In the blast furnace, coke (carbon) is burned with hot air to produce:

options.text: Carbon monoxide, which reduces the iron ore

mcq.explanation: Coke burns with hot air to produce carbon monoxide, which acts as the reducing agent that removes oxygen from the iron ore. Exam Tip: Carbon monoxide (CO) is the active reducing agent that removes oxygen from the iron ore, releasing molten iron.

mcq.questionText: The reduction of iron(III) oxide by carbon monoxide in the blast furnace can be summarised as:
mcq.explanation: Carbon monoxide removes oxygen from iron(III) oxide, forming molten iron and carbon dioxide: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Exam Tip: This equation shows REDUCTION of iron oxide (loses oxygen) and OXIDATION of carbon monoxide (gains oxygen, becomes CO2).

mcq.questionText: Limestone is added to the blast furnace mainly to:

options.text: Remove impurities (mainly silica/sand) by forming slag

mcq.explanation: Limestone decomposes and reacts with sandy silica impurities to form slag, which is removed from the furnace. Exam Tip: Limestone gives calcium oxide and carbon dioxide; calcium oxide then reacts with silica (impurity) to form calcium silicate (slag).

mcq.questionText: The waste material formed when limestone reacts with silica (sand) impurities in the blast furnace is called:
mcq.explanation: The waste material formed when limestone reacts with silica impurities is called slag, made mainly of calcium silicate. Exam Tip: Slag floats above the molten iron (being less dense) and is drawn off separately.

mcq.questionText: Molten iron collects at the bottom of the blast furnace mainly because it is:

options.text: Lighter than slag and floats on top
Denser than slag and sinks below it

mcq.explanation: Molten iron collects at the bottom of the blast furnace because it is denser than slag and sinks below it. Exam Tip: This density difference allows the two liquids (iron and slag) to be tapped off separately at different levels.

mcq.questionText: Coke serves TWO purposes in the blast furnace: as a fuel AND as a:
mcq.explanation: Coke serves two purposes: burning as a fuel to release heat, and forming carbon monoxide, which acts as a reducing agent. Exam Tip: Fuel (provides heat) plus reducing agent (removes oxygen from the ore) is coke's dual function and a key exam point.

mcq.questionText: Iron extracted directly from the blast furnace, containing several impurities (e.g. carbon), is called:
mcq.explanation: Iron extracted directly from the blast furnace, containing impurities such as carbon, is called pig iron (cast iron). Exam Tip: Pig iron is brittle due to impurities; it is later processed (e.g. into steel) for most practical uses.

mcq.questionText: Steel is essentially an alloy made mainly by:

options.text: Adding all the carbon back into pig iron
Removing most of the excess carbon and other impurities from pig iron, sometimes adding other elements

mcq.explanation: Steel is made by removing most of the excess carbon and other impurities from pig iron, sometimes with other elements added. Exam Tip: Steel has controlled, LOWER carbon content than pig iron, giving it better strength and flexibility.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a use of extracted iron and steel?

options.text: Construction of buildings, bridges, vehicles and tools

mcq.explanation: Iron and steel are widely used in the construction of buildings, bridges, vehicles and tools. Exam Tip: Iron and steel are foundational structural materials in modern infrastructure and industry.

mcq.questionText: The extraction of iron from its ore mainly involves the process of:

options.text: Reduction of iron oxide using carbon monoxide

mcq.explanation: The extraction of iron from its ore mainly involves the reduction of iron oxide using carbon monoxide. Exam Tip: The whole blast furnace process centres on this single reduction reaction.

mcq.questionText: Which raw material provides the heat energy needed to keep the blast furnace hot enough for the reactions to occur?
mcq.explanation: Burning coke with hot air releases the heat energy needed to keep the blast furnace hot enough for the reactions to occur. Exam Tip: Coke's combustion both heats the furnace AND generates the reducing agent (CO) - its dual role again.

fib.explanation: A naturally occurring rock from which a metal can be economically extracted is called an ore. Exam Tip: Haematite is the main iron ore.

fib.explanation: The main ore of iron is haematite, rich in iron(III) oxide. Exam Tip: Formula: Fe2O3.

fib.explanation: The industrial furnace used to extract iron from its ore is called the blast furnace. Exam Tip: A tall structure fed with ore, coke and limestone.

fib.explanation: In the blast furnace, coke burns with hot air to form carbon monoxide, the main reducing agent. Exam Tip: CO removes oxygen from iron(III) oxide.

fib.explanation: Limestone reacts with silica impurities in the furnace to form a waste product called slag. Exam Tip: Slag floats above molten iron and is removed separately.

fib.explanation: Coke serves as both a fuel and a reducing agent in the blast furnace. Exam Tip: It removes oxygen from the iron ore via carbon monoxide.

tf.questionText: Haematite is the main ore of iron.
tf.explanation: Haematite (Fe2O3) is indeed the principal iron ore, a reddish-brown iron-rich rock. Exam Tip: A reddish-brown iron-rich rock.

tf.questionText: Iron is extracted from its ore in a furnace called a kiln.
tf.explanation: Iron is extracted in a blast furnace, not a kiln; kilns are used for other processes such as cement or lime making. Exam Tip: Blast furnace equals iron extraction. Kiln is a different type of furnace.

tf.questionText: Coke burns with hot air in the blast furnace to produce carbon monoxide.
tf.explanation: This reaction forms carbon monoxide, the key reducing agent, which then reduces the iron ore further up the furnace. Exam Tip: This CO then reduces the iron ore further up the furnace.

tf.questionText: Limestone is added to the blast furnace to provide extra iron.
tf.explanation: Limestone's role is to remove impurities by reacting with silica to form slag, not to add iron. Exam Tip: Limestone leads to slag formation (impurity removal), not an iron source.

tf.questionText: Molten iron is denser than slag, so it sinks to the bottom of the furnace.
tf.explanation: Iron sinks below the less-dense slag, and this density difference allows the two liquids to be drawn off separately. Exam Tip: This allows the two liquids to be drawn off separately.

tf.questionText: Coke acts only as a fuel in the blast furnace and has no other role.
tf.explanation: Coke has two roles: fuel and reducing agent, since it also forms carbon monoxide which reduces the ore. Exam Tip: Don't overlook coke's second, equally important role as a reducing agent.

tf.questionText: Pig iron obtained directly from the blast furnace contains impurities such as carbon.
tf.explanation: Pig iron contains carbon and other impurities, which make it brittle and in need of further processing. Exam Tip: Pig iron needs further processing (e.g. into steel) for most uses.

tf.questionText: Steel is made by adding MORE carbon to pig iron.
tf.explanation: Steel-making removes excess carbon rather than adding more, giving steel its improved strength and properties. Exam Tip: Steel has LESS (controlled) carbon than pig iron - the statement reverses the process.

tf.questionText: The extraction of iron from its ore involves the reduction of iron oxide.
tf.explanation: Iron oxide loses oxygen (is reduced) to form iron metal, with carbon monoxide acting as the reducing agent. Exam Tip: Carbon monoxide is the reducing agent responsible.

tf.questionText: Iron and steel are widely used in the construction of buildings and bridges.
tf.explanation: Iron and steel are essential structural materials, and their strength and availability make them foundational to modern construction. Exam Tip: Strength and availability make iron/steel foundational to modern construction.

hoq.questionText: Describe, in order, what happens to the three raw materials (iron ore, coke, limestone) as they move down through a blast furnace, and explain how iron and slag end up being collected separately.

options.text: All three materials simply melt together with no chemical change

Coke burns with hot air to form carbon monoxide, which reduces the iron ore to molten iron; limestone decomposes and reacts with silica impurities to form slag; because molten iron is denser than slag, the two separate into layers and are tapped off at different levels
Limestone reduces the iron ore directly
Coke has no chemical role in the furnace

hoq.explanation: Coke burns with the hot air blast to form carbon monoxide, which then reduces the iron(III) oxide in the ore to molten iron (Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2). At the same time, limestone decomposes on heating (CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2) and the calcium oxide reacts with silica (sandy impurities) in the ore to form slag (calcium silicate). Since molten iron is denser than molten slag, the two liquids separate into distinct layers inside the furnace, with iron sinking below the slag, and both are then tapped off separately at different heights - molten iron from a lower outlet, slag from a higher one. Exam Tip: Three parallel processes happen together: reduction (coke/CO reduces ore), slag formation (limestone removes silica), and physical separation (density difference). A complete answer must connect all three - a single mechanism alone is incomplete.

hoq.questionText: A student argues that "coke is only useful in the blast furnace because it burns and provides heat." Evaluate this claim using the chemistry of the process.

options.text: The claim is incomplete: coke does provide heat by burning, but it ALSO reacts with the hot air to form carbon monoxide gas, which acts as the essential reducing agent that removes oxygen from the iron ore - without this second role, no iron metal would actually be produced
Coke has no chemical function at all
Coke's only role is to add carbon to the final iron

hoq.explanation: Coke does burn and release heat, keeping the furnace hot enough for all the reactions to proceed, so this part of the claim is correct. However, coke also reacts with the blast of hot air to generate carbon monoxide gas, and this carbon monoxide is the actual chemical agent that reduces iron(III) oxide to iron metal - without it, the iron ore would never be converted into metal, no matter how hot the furnace was. The claim is therefore incomplete: coke provides heat AND generates the reducing agent (carbon monoxide) that is essential for actually extracting the iron. Exam Tip: A classic half-true claim. Confirming coke's heating role while showing what is missing (its equally vital reducing-agent role) demonstrates full understanding of why coke is irreplaceable in this process - heat alone would just melt the ore, not extract the metal.

hoq.questionText: A factory receives a shipment of pig iron directly from a blast furnace and needs to convert it into a useful construction-grade steel. Explain the general chemical change required and why the pig iron cannot be used for construction as it is.

options.text: Nothing needs to change; pig iron is identical to steel

Pig iron contains too much carbon and other impurities, making it brittle and unsuitable for construction; it must be processed to remove most of the excess carbon and impurities, converting it into steel, which is stronger and more useful
Pig iron needs MORE carbon added to become steel
Pig iron should be melted with limestone only to form steel

hoq.explanation: Pig iron, straight from the blast furnace, contains a relatively high and uncontrolled level of carbon along with other impurities, and this high carbon content makes it hard but very brittle, unsuitable for structural uses that need strength combined with some flexibility. To make useful steel, most of the excess carbon (and other impurities) must be removed through further processing, giving a controlled, lower carbon content, so pig iron must be processed to remove excess carbon/impurities, converting it into steel - a stronger, less brittle alloy suitable for construction. Exam Tip: The key contrast is: pig iron equals high, uncontrolled carbon equals brittle; steel equals lower, controlled carbon (sometimes with other added elements) equals strong and versatile. This is why pig iron is always an intermediate product, never the final construction material.
